name: Front-to-back leg swing
form_cues: Hold a wall and stand tall on one leg.
Swing the free leg forward and back like a pendulum.
Let the range grow gradually with each swing.
common_mistakes: Rounding the lower back to fake range
Swinging wildly from the first rep
safety: Start small and build range; keep the swing controlled.
notes: Classic pre-run and pre-leg-day drill.

name: Lateral leg swing
form_cues: Face a wall with both hands on it.
Swing one leg across your body and out to the side.
Keep your hips and chest facing the wall.
common_mistakes: Twisting the torso with each swing
safety: Keep swings controlled; ease off if you feel groin pinching.

name: Arm circles
form_cues: Stand tall with arms straight out to the sides.
Draw small circles, then gradually make them bigger.
Reverse direction halfway through.
common_mistakes: Shrugging shoulders up to the ears
safety: Keep circles pain-free; shrink them if anything pinches.

name: World's greatest stretch
form_cues: Step into a long lunge and put both hands inside the front foot.
Drop the inside elbow toward the instep, then rotate that arm to the ceiling.
Finish by straightening the front leg to stretch the hamstring.
common_mistakes: Letting the back knee collapse to the floor
Rotating from the lower back instead of the upper back
safety: Move slowly; drop the back knee to the floor if balance is an issue.
notes: One of the best single warm-up drills: hips, hamstrings and upper back in one move.

name: Spiderman lunge
form_cues: From a push-up position, step one foot outside the same hand.
Sink the hips and reach that elbow toward the instep.
Step back and switch sides.
common_mistakes: Front heel lifting off the floor
safety: Keep the back leg long and core braced; stop if the groin pinches.

name: Inchworm
form_cues: Hinge forward and place hands on the floor, bending knees as needed.
Walk hands out to a plank, keeping hips level.
Walk hands back toward the feet and stand up.
common_mistakes: Letting the hips sag in the plank
Walking hands out too far for your strength
safety: Bend the knees as much as needed to protect your lower back.
notes: Add a push-up at the plank for a fuller warm-up.

name: Walking lunge with twist
form_cues: Step forward into a lunge with the front knee over the foot.
Rotate your chest toward the front leg.
Return to centre, then step through to the next lunge.
common_mistakes: Twisting from the knee instead of the torso
safety: Keep steps short if knees are sore; rotate from the ribs, not the knee.
notes: Hold a light plate or ball at the chest to add load.

name: Walking hip opener and closer
form_cues: Lift one knee high in front of you.
Rotate it out to the side and down (open), or side to front (close).
Stand tall and walk forward between reps.
common_mistakes: Leaning the torso to fake range
safety: Hold a wall for balance if needed; keep the movement smooth.

name: Frankenstein walk
form_cues: Walk forward kicking one straight leg up.
Reach the opposite hand toward the toes.
Keep your chest up and standing leg tall.
common_mistakes: Rounding the back to reach the toes
Kicking higher than your hamstrings allow
safety: Kick only to a comfortable height; this is a warm-up, not a max test.

name: Walking knee hug
form_cues: Step forward and pull one knee to your chest.
Rise onto the toes of the standing foot.
Release and step through to the other side.
common_mistakes: Rounding the back to meet the knee
safety: Hold a wall if balance is shaky.

name: Walking quad pull
form_cues: Step forward and grab the opposite ankle behind you.
Pull heel to glute and squeeze that glute.
Reach the free arm overhead for balance.
common_mistakes: Knee drifting out to the side
safety: Keep knees close together and avoid yanking the ankle.

name: Standing hip circles
form_cues: Stand with hands on hips and feet shoulder-width.
Draw big circles with your hips.
Keep your head and shoulders still.
safety: Keep the movement pain-free and controlled.

name: Ankle circles
form_cues: Lift one foot off the floor or sit with the leg extended.
Draw slow, full circles with your toes.
Change direction halfway.
common_mistakes: Moving the whole leg instead of the ankle
safety: Move only in a pain-free range after ankle sprains.

name: Wrist circles
form_cues: Interlock fingers or make loose fists.
Draw slow, full circles with the wrists.
Keep the forearms still.
common_mistakes: Moving the elbows instead of the wrists
safety: Keep it pain-free; useful before push-ups, handstands and pressing.

name: Quadruped wrist rocks
form_cues: Kneel on all fours with hands under shoulders.
Rock forward and back over the hands, keeping palms flat.
Repeat with fingers turned out, then with backs of hands down.
common_mistakes: Letting palms peel off the floor
safety: Shift less body weight onto the hands if wrists are sensitive.
notes: Great before handstands, push-ups and front squats.

name: Deep squat hold
form_cues: Sit down into the bottom of a squat, feet flat.
Push knees out with your elbows and lift your chest.
Shift side to side gently to explore the range.
safety: Hold onto something if heels lift; skip if deep knee flexion hurts.
notes: Raise heels on a plate if ankle mobility limits depth.

name: Scorpion stretch
form_cues: Lie face down with arms out wide.
Lift one leg and reach the foot toward the opposite hand.
Keep both shoulders as close to the floor as you can.
safety: Move slowly; skip if you have a disc problem or lower back pain.

name: Lumbar rotations
form_cues: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat.
Let both knees fall slowly to one side.
Keep shoulders flat and return through the middle.
safety: Move within a pain-free range; great gentle option for stiff backs.

name: Hip CARs
form_cues: Brace your core and lift one knee to hip height.
Rotate the knee out, open it to the side, then sweep the leg back.
Move as slowly as possible with zero movement in the torso.
common_mistakes: Moving fast to get through sticky spots
safety: Stay in a pain-free range and keep the trunk locked.
notes: From Functional Range Conditioning; also done on all fours.

name: Shoulder CARs
form_cues: Make a tight fist and brace your whole body.
Raise the arm forward and overhead as far as possible.
Rotate the thumb out and draw the biggest slow circle behind you.
common_mistakes: Arching the lower back or twisting to cheat range
safety: Keep everything but the working arm still; skip painful arcs.

name: Spinal CARs
form_cues: Stand tall with knees soft and squeeze your glutes lightly.
Curl down one vertebra at a time, starting at the neck.
Roll back up one segment at a time, then try side bends and rotation.
common_mistakes: Rushing so the spine moves as one block
safety: Go slowly and avoid if you have an acute disc injury.

name: 90/90 hip switch
form_cues: Sit with both knees bent to 90°, one leg in front and one to the side.
Keep feet planted and rotate both knees to the other side.
Sit tall; use hands behind you only if needed.
common_mistakes: Lifting the feet off the floor
safety: Use hand support if knees or hips are irritated.

name: 90/90 hip stretch
form_cues: Sit in the 90/90 position with both knees at right angles.
Sit tall and hinge your chest over the front shin.
Breathe slowly and relax into it.
common_mistakes: Rounding the back instead of hinging
safety: Prop the hip on a cushion if the knee feels strained.

name: Knee-to-wall ankle mobilization
form_cues: Stand facing a wall in a split stance, front toes a few cm away.
Drive the front knee toward the wall over the middle toes.
Keep the heel glued to the floor.
safety: Move the foot back as you improve; stop with sharp front-of-ankle pain.
notes: Doubles as a dorsiflexion test: aim for about 10 cm toe-to-wall.

name: Open book
form_cues: Lie on your side with knees bent to hip height and arms out front.
Open the top arm across, following it with your eyes.
Keep the knees stacked on the floor.
common_mistakes: Forcing the arm to the floor
safety: Squeeze a pillow between knees to keep the lower back still.

name: Quadruped thoracic rotation
form_cues: Kneel on all fours and sit the hips slightly back.
Place one hand behind your head.
Rotate that elbow down under the body, then up toward the ceiling.
safety: Sitting back toward the heels keeps the movement in the upper back.

name: Wall slide
form_cues: Put forearms on a wall at shoulder height.
Slide them up, letting shoulder blades wrap around the ribs.
Lower slowly back down.
safety: Stay below any pinching point in the shoulder.
notes: Add a loop band around the wrists for more rotator cuff work.

name: Wall angel
form_cues: Stand with head, upper back and glutes against a wall.
Hold arms in a W with backs of hands on the wall.
Slide arms up and down without anything lifting away.
common_mistakes: Lower back arching off the wall
Hands peeling away from the wall
safety: Step feet farther out if you can't keep your back flat.

name: Adductor rock-back
form_cues: Kneel on all fours and straighten one leg out to the side.
Rock hips back toward your heel.
Keep your back flat and return forward.
safety: Keep the range comfortable on the groin.

name: Active straight leg raise
form_cues: Lie on your back with both legs straight.
Raise one straight leg as high as you can without help.
Press the other leg firmly into the floor.
common_mistakes: Bottom leg lifting off the floor
safety: Keep the lower back flat; useful as a hamstring mobility check.

name: Couch stretch
form_cues: Kneel with your back shin up a wall or couch.
Step the other foot forward and squeeze the back glute.
Lift your chest slowly toward upright.
common_mistakes: Kneeling right on the kneecap without padding
safety: Pad the knee well and back off if the knee hurts.

name: Bretzel stretch
form_cues: Lie on your side, top knee bent at hip height and pinned down.
Grab the bottom foot behind you with your top hand.
Rotate your chest and shoulders toward the floor behind you.
safety: Use a strap on the back foot if you can't reach it.

name: Kneeling hip flexor stretch
form_cues: Kneel on one knee with the other foot forward.
Tuck your pelvis and squeeze the back glute.
Shift your weight forward until you feel the front of the hip.
common_mistakes: Lunging far without tucking the pelvis
safety: Pad the knee; you should feel it in the hip, not the lower back.
notes: Reach the same-side arm overhead for a stronger stretch.

name: Standing quad stretch
form_cues: Stand tall and grab one ankle behind you.
Pull the heel toward your glute, knees together.
Tuck your pelvis gently to feel more in the hip.
common_mistakes: Knee flaring out to the side
safety: Hold a wall for balance; don't yank the ankle.

name: Standing hamstring stretch
form_cues: Put one heel on a low step with the leg straight.
Keep your back flat and hinge forward from the hips.
Point the toes up for more stretch.
common_mistakes: Rounding the back to reach down
safety: Use a lower step if you feel it behind the knee rather than the thigh.

name: Seated single-leg hamstring stretch
form_cues: Sit with one leg straight and the other foot against the inner thigh.
Hinge forward from the hips toward the straight leg's foot.
Keep your chest long rather than curling down.
safety: Sit on a cushion if your lower back rounds a lot.

name: Wall calf stretch
form_cues: Put your hands on a wall with one leg back and straight.
Press the back heel down, toes pointing forward.
Lean your hips toward the wall.
safety: Ease in gradually if you have Achilles pain.

name: Bent-knee soleus stretch
form_cues: Stand in a short split stance facing a wall.
Bend both knees and sink the back knee toward the floor.
Keep the back heel down.
common_mistakes: Standing too far from the wall
safety: Back off if the Achilles feels sharp rather than stretched.

name: Supine figure-four stretch
form_cues: Lie on your back and cross one ankle over the other knee.
Pull the bottom thigh toward your chest.
Gently push the crossed knee away to deepen it.
safety: Flex the crossed foot to protect the knee.

name: Doorway chest stretch
form_cues: Place your forearm on a doorframe with elbow at shoulder height.
Step through with the same-side leg.
Turn your chest slightly away until you feel the chest open.
safety: Keep the elbow at or below shoulder height to protect the shoulder joint.
notes: Raise the elbow higher to bias the lower pec.

name: Doorframe lat stretch
form_cues: Grab a doorframe at hip height with one hand.
Sit your hips back and away, letting the side body lengthen.
Rotate slightly to find the tightest spot.
safety: Make sure the post you hold is solid.

name: Overhead triceps stretch
form_cues: Raise one arm and bend the elbow so your hand drops behind your head.
Use the other hand to ease the elbow back.
Keep your ribs down.
safety: Ease off if you feel pinching at the top of the shoulder.

name: Cross-body shoulder stretch
form_cues: Bring one straight arm across your chest.
Pull it in at the upper arm with the other hand.
Keep the shoulder down, away from the ear.
safety: Pull above the elbow, not on the joint.

name: Sleeper stretch
form_cues: Lie on your side with the bottom arm out at 90°, elbow bent.
Use the top hand to press the forearm gently toward the floor.
Roll back slightly to ease pressure on the shoulder.
common_mistakes: Lying directly on the point of the shoulder
safety: Very gentle pressure only; stop with any sharp front-of-shoulder pain.
notes: Popular with throwers and racquet-sport players.

name: Upper trap stretch
form_cues: Sit tall and hold the chair with one hand.
Tilt your ear toward the opposite shoulder.
Rest the other hand on your head for light extra pull.
safety: Use only light hand pressure; stop with tingling in the arm.

name: Levator scapulae stretch
form_cues: Turn your nose toward your armpit.
Gently pull your head down with the same-side hand.
Hold the opposite shoulder down.
safety: Keep pressure gentle; neck stretches should never feel sharp.

name: Chin tucks
form_cues: Sit or stand tall looking straight ahead.
Slide your chin straight back to make a double chin.
Hold 2–3 seconds and relax.
common_mistakes: Tipping the head down instead of sliding back
progressions: Supine chin tuck with head lift
safety: Stop if you get dizziness or arm symptoms.
notes: Good counter to 'tech neck' posture.

name: Wrist flexor stretch
form_cues: Hold one arm out straight, palm up.
Gently pull the fingers back with the other hand.
Keep the elbow straight.
safety: Stop with numbness or tingling in the fingers.

name: Wrist extensor stretch
form_cues: Hold one arm out straight, palm down.
Gently press the back of the hand toward you.
Keep the elbow straight.
safety: Helpful for tennis-elbow type tightness; keep it gentle.

name: Butterfly stretch
form_cues: Sit with the soles of your feet together.
Hold your feet and sit tall.
Let the knees drop; hinge forward a little for more.
safety: Don't push the knees down with force.

name: Side lunge adductor stretch
form_cues: Stand with feet wide.
Shift into one bent knee, keeping the other leg straight.
Keep both feet flat and chest up.
common_mistakes: Straight-leg foot rolling onto its edge
safety: Keep the bent knee tracking over the toes.

name: Standing IT band stretch
form_cues: Cross one leg behind the other.
Push the hip of the back leg out to the side.
Reach the same arm overhead and lean away.
safety: Hold a wall for balance.
notes: The IT band itself barely stretches; this mainly targets the TFL and glute.

name: Kneeling shin stretch
form_cues: Kneel with the tops of your feet flat on the floor.
Sit back toward your heels.
Lift the knees slightly for more stretch.
safety: Use a cushion under the knees; skip if kneeling hurts.
notes: Useful for shin splints.

name: Seated plantar fascia stretch
form_cues: Sit and cross one foot over the other knee.
Pull your toes back toward your shin.
Feel along the arch with the other thumb.
common_mistakes: Pulling the ankle instead of the toes
safety: Great first thing in the morning for plantar fasciitis.

name: Towel internal rotation stretch
form_cues: Hold a towel overhead with one hand and behind your back with the other.
Pull up with the top hand to raise the lower hand.
Keep shoulders relaxed.
safety: Gentle pull only; common in shoulder rehab programmes.

name: PNF hamstring stretch
form_cues: Lie down with one leg raised; a partner or strap holds it at a stretch.
Push the leg down into resistance for 6 seconds.
Relax, breathe out and ease the leg higher; repeat.
common_mistakes: Partner forcing the leg past comfort
safety: Contract at moderate effort; communicate clearly with your partner.
notes: Proprioceptive neuromuscular facilitation: contract 6 sec, relax, then stretch 20–30 sec.

name: PNF chest stretch
form_cues: Set up in the doorway chest stretch.
Press the forearm into the frame for 6 seconds.
Relax, step through a little deeper and hold.
safety: Keep the elbow at or below shoulder height.

name: PNF adductor stretch
form_cues: Sit in a butterfly with hands on the inner knees.
Press knees up into your hands for 6 seconds.
Relax and let the knees fall a little lower.
safety: Gentle hand pressure only; never push through groin pain.

name: Scap push-up
form_cues: Hold a plank on hands with straight arms.
Let your chest sink between the shoulder blades.
Push the floor away to spread the shoulder blades.
safety: Keep the elbows locked; the movement is only at the shoulder blades.

name: Prone Y-T-W raise
form_cues: Lie face down with your forehead on a towel.
Lift your arms into a Y, then a T, then a W.
Squeeze shoulder blades down and back each time.
common_mistakes: Lifting the chest off the floor
safety: Use thumbs up and light or no weight.
notes: Add 0.5–2 kg plates or dumbbells to progress.

name: Eccentric heel drop
form_cues: Stand on a step and rise up on both feet.
Shift onto one foot and lower the heel slowly below the step.
Use both feet to come back up.
common_mistakes: Dropping fast instead of lowering slowly
safety: Mild tendon discomfort is common; stop if pain is sharp or worsening.
notes: Classic Achilles tendinopathy protocol; do with straight and bent knee.

name: Short foot exercise
form_cues: Sit or stand with the foot flat.
Draw the ball of the foot toward the heel to lift the arch.
Keep the toes long and relaxed.
safety: Gentle and safe; useful for flat feet and plantar pain.

name: Prone press-up
form_cues: Lie face down with hands under your shoulders.
Press your chest up, letting the hips and belly stay on the floor.
Relax your lower back and lower slowly.
common_mistakes: Squeezing the glutes and lifting the hips
safety: Stop if leg pain spreads further down; see a professional for disc issues.
notes: Part of the McKenzie method for some back pain types.

name: Sciatic nerve floss
form_cues: Sit tall at the edge of a chair.
Straighten one knee while you look up.
Bend the knee as you look down; keep it smooth.
common_mistakes: Holding at end range like a stretch
safety: Should feel mild; stop if symptoms increase or linger.
notes: Nerves like movement, not long holds.

name: 90/90 breathing
form_cues: Lie on your back with feet on a wall, hips and knees at 90°.
Breathe in through the nose into the ribs and belly.
Exhale fully through the mouth and pause.
safety: Very safe; a good post-workout cool-down to calm the nervous system.

name: Strap hamstring stretch
form_cues: Lie on your back with a strap around one foot.
Raise the straight leg until you feel a stretch.
Keep the other leg flat on the floor.
common_mistakes: Bending the raised knee a lot
safety: Use a towel if you don't have a strap.

name: Strap prone quad stretch
form_cues: Lie face down with a strap looped around one ankle.
Pull the heel toward your glute.
Press the hip into the floor.
safety: Ease the strap in slowly.

name: Strap adductor stretch
form_cues: Lie on your back with a strap on one foot, leg straight up.
Lower the leg out to the side.
Keep the opposite hip pinned down.
safety: Lower only as far as your hips stay level.

name: Band shoulder dislocate
form_cues: Hold a band wide with straight arms in front.
Lift it overhead and behind you in one smooth arc.
Bring it back the same way.
safety: Start with a wide grip and narrow it gradually.
notes: A PVC pipe or broomstick works too.

name: Banded lat stretch
form_cues: Loop a band around a high anchor and your wrist.
Step back and sit your hips back.
Let the band pull your arm overhead and to the side.
safety: Use a secure anchor; check the band for tears.

name: Banded hip distraction
form_cues: Loop a heavy band around the top of your thigh from a low anchor.
Step away into a kneeling lunge or all-fours position.
Rock gently into the stretch.
common_mistakes: Band sliding down to the knee
safety: Anchor must be solid; band high in the hip crease.

name: Banded ankle distraction
form_cues: Loop a band around the front of the ankle, anchored behind you.
Step forward into a half-kneel.
Drive the knee forward over the toes; the band pulls the ankle back.
common_mistakes: Band on the foot, not the ankle crease
safety: Avoid after a recent sprain without clearance.

name: Band external rotation
form_cues: Hold a band at elbow height with the elbow tucked at your side.
Rotate the forearm outward, keeping the elbow pinned.
Return slowly.
common_mistakes: Elbow drifting away from the body
safety: Light band; a rolled towel under the arm helps keep form.

name: Band internal rotation
form_cues: Anchor a band at elbow height to the side of the working arm.
Pull the forearm across your stomach.
Keep the elbow tucked against your side.
safety: Light resistance; stop if the front of the shoulder hurts.

name: Terminal knee extension
form_cues: Loop a band behind your knee from an anchor in front.
Start with the knee slightly bent.
Squeeze the quad to straighten the knee fully.
safety: Keep it pain-free; common after knee surgery.

name: Foam roll legs and back
form_cues: Roll slowly, about 2–3 cm per second.
Pause 20–30 seconds on tender spots and breathe.
Spend 30–60 seconds on each area.
common_mistakes: Rolling directly on joints or the lower back
safety: Avoid bony areas, the lower back and the neck.
notes: General routine; see individual entries for each area.

name: Foam roll quads
form_cues: Lie face down with the roller under your thighs.
Roll from just above the knee to the hip.
Turn slightly in and out to hit inner and outer quads.
safety: Keep your core braced to protect the lower back.

name: Foam roll hamstrings
form_cues: Sit with the roller under your thighs and hands behind you.
Lift your hips and roll from knee to glute.
Cross one leg over the other for more pressure.
safety: Avoid the back of the knee.

name: Foam roll calves
form_cues: Sit with the roller under your calves.
Lift your hips and roll from ankle to knee.
Turn the foot in and out to hit each side.
safety: Stack one leg on top for more pressure.

name: Foam roll IT band
form_cues: Lie on your side with the roller under the outer thigh.
Use the top leg and hands to control pressure.
Roll from hip to just above the knee.
common_mistakes: Putting full body weight on it
safety: This area is sensitive; reduce pressure with the top foot.

name: Foam roll glutes
form_cues: Sit on the roller and cross one ankle over the other knee.
Lean toward the crossed-leg side.
Roll slowly over the glute.
safety: Stay on the meaty glute area, away from the tailbone.

name: Foam roll thoracic spine
form_cues: Lie with the roller under your upper back, hands behind your head.
Roll from mid-back to the shoulder blades.
Pause and gently extend over the roller at stiff spots.
common_mistakes: Flaring ribs and arching from the lower back
safety: Never roll the lumbar spine; support your head.

name: Foam roll lats
form_cues: Lie on your side with the roller under your armpit, arm overhead.
Roll down toward the bottom of the ribs.
Rotate slightly forward and back.
common_mistakes: Rolling onto the ribs too hard
safety: Keep the head supported on the arm.

name: Foam roll chest
form_cues: Lie face down with the roller at an angle under one side of the chest.
Extend that arm out to the side.
Roll slowly from the breastbone toward the shoulder.
safety: Light pressure; avoid the front of the shoulder joint.

name: Stability ball back stretch
form_cues: Sit on a stability ball and walk your feet forward.
Lie back so the ball supports your upper and mid back.
Reach your arms overhead and relax.
safety: Keep feet wide for balance; avoid if you get dizzy.

name: Massage ball glute release
form_cues: Sit or lie with the ball under one glute.
Find a tender spot and let your weight sink in.
Breathe and make small circles.
common_mistakes: Rolling on the sciatic nerve with sharp, shooting pain
safety: Move off any spot that causes numbness or shooting pain.
notes: Do it against a wall for less pressure.

name: Massage ball foot roll
form_cues: Stand or sit with the ball under one foot.
Roll from heel to toes with steady pressure.
Pause on tender spots.
common_mistakes: Standing with full weight straight away
safety: A frozen water bottle works for sore arches.

name: Massage ball pec release
form_cues: Stand facing a wall with the ball under your chest, just inside the shoulder.
Lean in to apply pressure.
Slowly move the arm up and down.
common_mistakes: Pressing on the collarbone or armpit nerves
safety: Stay on soft tissue; stop with tingling down the arm.

name: Massage ball upper back release
form_cues: Stand against a wall or lie with the ball between spine and shoulder blade.
Lean into the ball at a tender spot.
Cross the arm over your chest to open the area.
common_mistakes: Putting the ball on the spine
safety: Keep the ball off the spine and the neck.

name: Massage ball TFL release
form_cues: Lie face down with the ball just in front of and below the hip bone.
Let your weight sink in.
Bend and straighten the knee slowly.
common_mistakes: Lying on it with full weight from the start
safety: Avoid the groin area and front-of-hip nerves.

name: Massage ball forearm release
form_cues: Place the ball on a table under your forearm.
Press down with the other hand.
Open and close your fist as you roll.
safety: Good for climbers, lifters with grippy forearms and desk workers.

name: Side-lying dumbbell external rotation
form_cues: Lie on your side with the top elbow bent at 90° on your hip.
Rotate the dumbbell up toward the ceiling.
Lower slowly.
common_mistakes: Lifting the elbow off the side
safety: Use 1–3 kg; place a towel between elbow and ribs.

name: Bench lat stretch
form_cues: Kneel facing a bench with elbows on the edge.
Bend the elbows so your hands meet behind your head (or hold a dowel).
Sit hips back and let the chest sink.
safety: Keep ribs down; stop with shoulder pinching.
notes: Great prep for overhead squats and presses.

name: Cable external rotation
form_cues: Set a cable at elbow height and stand side-on.
Keep the elbow tucked and rotate the forearm out.
Return slowly against the cable.
safety: Keep it light; this is a control exercise.

name: Cable internal rotation
form_cues: Set a cable at elbow height, cable on the working-arm side.
Keep the elbow pinned and rotate the forearm across your body.
Return slowly.
safety: Light load; stop with front-of-shoulder pain.
